name: Autosomal Recessive Disease with Focal Palmoplantar Keratoderma

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic Criteria for Autosomal Recessive Focal Palmoplantar Keratoderma

criteria.description: Presence of focal palmoplantar keratoderma with well-demarcated hyperkeratotic plaques
Confirmed autosomal recessive inheritance pattern by family history or genetic testing
Identification of pathogenic variants in associated gene(s) linked to focal palmoplantar keratoderma
Exclusion of other keratoderma types such as diffuse or punctate forms
Skin biopsy showing epidermal hyperplasia and orthokeratotic hyperkeratosis

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of focal palmoplantar keratoderma plus autosomal recessive inheritance pattern and/or genetic confirmation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing is strongly recommended to confirm diagnosis and differentiate from other keratoderma disorders.

laboratory: Skin biopsy showing epidermal hyperplasia and orthokeratotic hyperkeratosis
Negative fungal cultures in most cases
genetic: Pathogenic variants in genes associated with keratinization disorders (e.g., KRT9, KRT1 mutations)
Autosomal recessive inheritance confirmed by genetic testing
other: Clinical observation of well-demarcated focal keratoderma plaques
Family history consistent with autosomal recessive transmission

distinguishingFeatures: Multiple small hyperkeratotic papules rather than plaques
Onset typically in adolescence or adulthood

redFlags: Presence of blistering or erosions suggesting epidermolysis
Signs of secondary infection such as purulence or systemic symptoms
